title: Anchor-and-freeze-model-reference-semantics-for-sdk-api
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define and implement SDK + API semantics for anchoring (freeze) model references by tag, semver range, or commit hash. Provide clear resolution precedence, backward-compatible defaults, and graceful runtime fallbacks tied to published performance profiles. Deliver SDK surface, server-side resolver rules, migration path for existing callers, and telemetry to detect unintended upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: SDK accepts model_reference with optional anchorMode and anchorSelector parameters
Server resolver implements deterministic precedence: exact-commit -> semver-exact -> semver-range (highest satisfying) -> time-bound floating-tag -> latest-family-fallback
Anchors marked 'frozen' return HTTP 409 on incompatible replacement attempts in control plane for 30-day stability window
Runtime publishes resolution trace headers (X-Redwood-Model-Resolved, X-Redwood-Resolve-Reason) and metrics (resolution_path, fallback_count)
CLI and SDK migration guide and quick-fix warnings for callers relying on implicit 'latest' behavior
E2E tests cover canary, frozen anchor replacement, semver-range upgrades, and downgrade rejections
notes: Terminology: use 'anchor' for a user-facing stable reference and 'freeze' to denote a non-auto-updating anchor; avoid the word 'pin' in public SDK to reduce user confusion with package pinning semantics.

Anchor modes: 'frozen' (never auto-updates), 'floating' (resolves to tag head but with a stability window), 'canary' (resolves to candidate variant with explicit acceptance), default is 'floating' for backwards compatibility.

Resolution precedence: exact commit hash >= semver exact tag >= semver range (select highest satisfying release with published performance profile) >= floating tag head (bounded by stability window) >= model-family latest (if all else fails). This order ensures reproducibility when callers provide stronger constraints.

Semver handling: support ^, ~, ranges, and exact versions. For ranges pick the highest available release that has a published performance profile compatible with requested workload hints (sequence length, batching).

Performance profile lookup: resolver must consult performance_profile metadata to avoid auto-resolving to a variant that doesn't meet caller constraints (latency SLO, memory cap). If no compatible profile exists, resolver should fall back and emit a warning trace and metric.
Stability window: floating anchors adopt a 72-hour propagation and 30-day soft-stability window where a change emits warnings and requires explict control-plane override to replace.

Control-plane guardrails: attempting to replace a 'frozen' anchor within its stability window returns a controlled rejection and an audit log entry. Allow an explicit override flag for emergency replacements that creates an incident ticket automatically.

SDK ergonomics: propose API: model_reference: string, anchor_mode?: string ('frozen'|'floating'|'canary'), anchor_selector?: string (commit|semver|tag), resolver_hints?: string (workload:low_latency|high_throughput), resolve_timeout_ms?: number. Provide helper constructors in JS and Python clients.

Migration: add deprecation warnings in server for callers that pass bare model name without anchorSelector; communicate default remains 'floating' for 6 months then require explicit anchor_selector in major SDK release.

Telemetry: emit resolution_reason tags (exact, semver_exact, semver_range, tag_head, family_fallback) plus histograms for resolution latency and counts for fallback events. Add alert if fallback_count spikes >5% for a customer.
Security: no additional secrets exposure. Audit logs for anchor replacements must include actor, reason, and resulting resolved ref.

testing_notes: Unit: resolver precedence matrix with mocked model catalog (commit, semver exact, semver range, tag head)
Integration: end-to-end requests with anchors in hosted and dedicated environments verifying headers and fallback metric emission
Chaos: attempt concurrent anchor replacements to validate control-plane guard rejects and audit entry creation
Performance: measure resolver latency added to request path; target <3ms median for cache hit, <15ms cold
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): server+SDK behind feature flag for internal customers and a small set of beta tenants (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (gradual): enable default floating anchors and telemetry for all hosted customers; keep deprecated warning for bare model names (4 weeks)
Phase 3 (enforce): require explicit anchor_selector in new SDK major release; keep backward compatibility for existing tokens for 6 months
Emergency rollback: control-plane override and incident workflow that documents replaced anchors and triggers postmortem
